sentences.text:
The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 20.06.2023.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 20.03.2023 at about 11.00am the Petitioner was an occupant traveling in the BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57- F-0511 from Narayanapura Cross towards Nagavara.

While so proceeding the BMTC bus driver has driven the bus in a rash and negligent manner endangering human life came with high speed without observing any of the traffic rules, reached near Thanisandra Railway bridge, Thanisandra main road, Bangalore city, the driver lost control over the bus and dashed the bus to the Iron Pole.
As a result of the forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Prakruthi Multi Specialty Hospital, Thanisandra Main Road, Bangalore - 77, provided first aid treatment and admitted as an inpatient from 20.06.2023 to 22.06.2023 for about 3 days, surgery was done and necessary treatment was offered and discharged with an advice for complete bed rest.

entities.text: Prakruthi Multi Specialty Hospital, Thanisandra Main Road,
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: So far he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medicines and Rs.50,000/- towards incidental expenses.

4. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, prior to the date of accident he was hale and healthy and working as Software Engineer at Executive Software Guild and earning Rs.6,75,844/- per month.
Due to grievous injuries, prolonged treatment the petitioner could not attend to his work and lost income.
The petitioner has also undergone untold mental shock and agony.
The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-0511.
The Hennur Traffic Police have registered a case against the Driver of the Said bus in Cr.No.87/2023 p/u/Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
The Respondent being the RC owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.
5. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondent appeared and filed written statement.

6. The objections of the Respondent:
It has denied the rashness and negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0511, the accident and grievous injuries to the petitioner.

Further stated that on 20.06.2023, on route from Mylanahalli to Shivajinagar, on the route at about 11.05am the bus reached on boot factory bus stand, the Passengers were deboarding the bus and some passengers were boarding the bus.
The bus stationed in the bus stand waiting for the passengers to get down and to board the bus.
At that time suddenly there was jerk to the bus resulting in sudden movement of the bus without notice of the bus driver.

However, the bus driver made his efforts to Akhilesh Kumra Jaiswal vs B.M.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114872928/
2 halt the bus by applying hand break and break.

sentences.text: However, the bus moved towards center of the road and hit railway pole to the railway bridge, causing damages to the Bus and some passengers were injured due to sudden jerk to the bus.
Thereafter the bus driver got the passengers admitted to the nearby hospital for treatment.
The freak accident is due to the severe jerk to the bus without notice of the bus driver.
The bus driver is not negligent in driving the bus and was careful and was driving the Bus by observing traffic rules.
It has denied the nature of accident, involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Further denied the age, income, avocation of the petitioner.
It has contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 20.06.2023 at 11.00am due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-0511 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for Compensation?

If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
8.
The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 16 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.16.
He has also got examined Mr. S. Karthik - Medical Record Department Officer as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.17 to P.20.

On the other side, the Respondent examined its Driver Mr.Devaraj as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 & R.2.
9.
Heard the arguments of the learned counsels for both the parties.

10. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS  11. Issue No.1:
In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the Driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-0511 the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 8 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 8.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination.

The Respondent has denied the rash and Akhilesh Kumra Jaiswal vs B.M.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114872928/
3

sentences.text: negligent driving by the driver of the said bus.
In the cross-examination of PW.1, he has stated that he was sitting next to the back side door.
The width of the Road was 60 feet, Cement Road and there is a divider of 3 feet height.
12. In support of the defence the respondent has got examined its Driver as RW.1 and produced 2 documents as per Exs.R.1 & R.2.
In the cross-examination, he has admitted that the chargesheet is filed against him.

13. Ex.P.5 MVA report reveals that the Bus was damaged to its (i) Front Bumper pressed and damaged,
(ii) Bonnet dislocated, (iii) Radiator pressed and damaged (iv) wind shield glass broken (v) left side head lamp glass and indicator glass broken (vi) front shape of the MV pressed and damaged (vii) front left side corner of the body pressed and damaged (viii)
front left side door dislocated (ix) rear glass broken and (x) front dashboard pressed inwards.
The other documents at Exs.P.1 to P.8 i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report and charge sheet are in accordance with the statement given by the petitioner.
No contrary evidence is led against these documents from the side of respondent.

As such, there are no reasons to discard or disbelieve the version of the Petitioner/PW.1.
14.
As per Ex.P.7/Wound Certificate, the petitioner sustained injuries on 20.06.2023 in a RTA.
This shows that on account of the accident the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

The respondent has contended that the petitioner was negligent since he did not heed to the instructions given by the driver and the conductor about the brake not working and was busy talking on the phone even when all the other passengers were holding on tight to the bus.
But the respondent has not produced any document even though RW.1 has claimed that the Bus had camera.
The driver claims that he could not apply brake suddenly but the IMV report at Ex.P.5 shows that the vehicle did not have any technical defect.

Therefore, on overall perusal of Exs.P.1 to 8 it is clear that the accident occurred on 20.06.2023 and the petitioner sustained injuries as mentioned in Ex.P.7 and the sole reason for the occurrence of the accident was rash and negligent driving by the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0511.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.

15. Issue No.2:-
The Petitioner has further averred that on account of the accident he has suffered injuries to upper, lower eyelid soft tissue injury upto lateral commisure nasal bone fracture with suptal fracture which are grievous in nature, could be seen at Ex.P.7.
In this regard he has examined Medical Record Keeper Mr.S.Karthik as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.17 to 20, authorization letter, police intimation, MLC register extract and case sheet.
During the cross examination of PW.2, nothing worthwhile is elicited.

The Petitioner to substantiate the there is loss of income due to the accidental injuries and that he is suffering from permanent disability has not examined either the treated Doctor or any other Doctor who has got expertise in this field.

He also has Akhilesh Kumra Jaiswal vs B.M.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114872928/
4 not placed any disability certificate issued by the competent person to prove that he suffered permanent disability.

sentences.text: Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused him permanent disability resulting in loss of income and accordingly the version of the petitioner in this regard is not acceptable.
Under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
However, it is pertinent to note that, the wound certificate produced as per Ex.P.7 discloses that, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of Pain and Suffering.

The Petitioner has stated that he has spent more than Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical,
conveyance and nourishment expenses.
In this regard he has produced 25 medical bills for Rs.1,25,468/- as per Ex.P.10.
There is no contrary evidence to this document from the respondents.

As such, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.1,25,468/-
under the head of medical expenses.
As mentioned above the Petitioner was treated at Prakruthi Multispeciality Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was treated from 20.06.2023 to 22.06.2023 for 3 days.
In this regard he has produced discharge summary of Prakruthi Multi Speciality Hospital at Ex.P.9.
During that time, certainly he would have spent some amount towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and for other incidental expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and other incidental expenses.
The total compensation comes to Rs.1,85,468/-.
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.1,85,500/-.
LIABILITY 16.
The Respondent in the written statement has specifically denied the rash and negligent of the driver of the BMTC Bus, but has not proved the same.
Therefore, the Respondent being the RC Owner is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, the Respondent has stated that it has paid Rs.10,000/- as interim compensation to the petitioner.
In this regard it has produced Ex.R.2, it has to be deducted while compensating the petitioner.

The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.18,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.1,75,500/- (Rs.1,85,500/- -
Rs.10,000/- = Rs.1,75,500/-) with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues this court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.1,75,500/- (Rupees One Akhilesh Kumra Jaiswal vs B.M.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114872928/
5 Lakh Seventy Five Thousand Five Hundred only) from the Respondents along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondent is liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
